The British Council Scholarships for Women in STEM fund selected one-year master’s degrees in the UK for women who need financial support. The package covers tuition fees and helps with living, travel and other study costs.

Applications for 2026-27 are closed. If you are planning for 2027-28, start preparing your academic documents and course shortlist, but wait for official confirmation of the next eligible countries, universities and deadlines. The previous cycle offers useful guidance, not a guaranteed place in the next one.

What is the British Council Women in STEM scholarship?

The programme supports women in science, technology, engineering and mathematics who want to develop their expertise through postgraduate study. It also encourages scholars to use that experience at home and help more women and girls enter STEM.

British Council Women in STEM scholarship eligibility

The official criteria for the 2026-27 academic year provide the starting point. Applicants needed to:

  • Meet the programme’s definition of a woman and its documentation requirements.
  • Meet eligible-country residence and travel-document rules.
  • Meet their chosen course’s academic and English-language requirements.
  • Show financial need and relevant STEM experience or a clear interest in the subject.

Scholars also committed to returning to their country of citizenship or residence for at least two years, subject to exceptional circumstances, and supporting women and girls in STEM.

Who cannot apply, and which restrictions need checking?

Check your course as carefully as your personal eligibility. An offer for a different programme, a different study mode or an unlisted start date does not establish scholarship eligibility. Use the institution's exact award conditions before paying a deposit or accepting an offer on that assumption.

Previous UK study needs particular care. The general rules expressed a preference for applicants without significant international study, while Queen Mary also published restrictions on previous UK degree-level study or recent UK residence. If the conditions appear to conflict, ask the university before assuming you qualify.

English requirements need a separate check. Compare the language evidence your chosen course accepts, then confirm its required scores and submission deadline directly. An award that covers an IELTS fee does not automatically waive English proficiency requirements.

Eligible countries for British Council Women in STEM scholarships

For the South Asia awards discussed below, the 2026-27 university pages listed Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Applicants still needed to satisfy the relevant residence, academic and financial conditions.

These five countries were not the programme’s entire international reach. The previous cycle also included regional arrangements such as ASEAN-UK SAGE and separately supported cohorts for Hong Kong, Mexico and Brazil, as described in the criteria linked above. Each route had its own scope.

For 2027-28, check three things together: your country, the participating university and the exact course. A country name on a British Council website’s worldwide navigation menu is not proof of scholarship eligibility.

Is Nigeria eligible for the British Council STEM scholarship?

Nigeria does not appear in the five-country South Asia lists covered here. Those lists alone do not establish eligibility for every regional award, and the sources reviewed do not confirm a 2027-28 route for Nigerian applicants.

How to apply for the British Council STEM scholarship

When the next round opens, follow your chosen university’s instructions. Do not assume one central application covers every institution.

  1. Confirm your route. Match your country and circumstances to an eligible university and programme.
  2. Check the sequence. Find out whether you need a course application, an offer or a separate scholarship form first.
  3. Prepare a specific case. Explain your financial need, relevant experience and intended contribution after study.
  4. Submit every required component. Keep confirmation emails and monitor the university portal for requests.

Do not leave portal access until the final evening. Edinburgh’s guidance allows up to five working days after an admission application for system checks and scholarship access.

Preparing your scholarship application answers

If you are applying from Pakistan, Bangladesh or another eligible country, use the questions in your chosen university’s current form. Prepare specific evidence of financial need, your STEM work, course fit and plans after returning home.

For example, a civil engineering graduate could connect a drainage project to further study in flood resilience, then describe how she would share that knowledge with local women engineers. Explain what you actually did and what you want to learn next.

That is a preparation example, not an official application question. Build on it by turning your experience into a focused statement, with specific actions rather than broad claims about passion.

Keep a separate folder for the scholarship form and financial-need evidence. The institution’s current instructions determine what you must submit, so avoid treating a previous applicant’s checklist as a universal requirement.

Check whether the university requires translations of documents that are not in English. Keep names and dates consistent across your records, and ask your referees early enough to avoid a last-minute submission problem.

How scholarship applications are assessed

The published university criteria look beyond whether you hold a degree. They ask for financial need, motivation, relevant STEM experience or interest, and a credible contribution after study. Eligibility gets you into consideration; it does not guarantee selection.

Use these preparation questions to test your answers. They are editorial prompts, not an official scoring system:

  • Financial need: have you explained the gap between the cost of study and the resources realistically available to you?
  • Course fit: can you connect a particular skill you need with your chosen programme?
  • STEM evidence: what project, work, research or other relevant activity shows your commitment?

Then explain what happens after graduation. For example, identify a home-country problem you want to address and a practical way to involve other women or girls in that work. A realistic mentoring or training plan gives the reader something concrete to assess.

The universities manage application enquiries and communicate their decisions. If you already applied for 2026-27, contact the institution with your applicant ID and course name; a new article update cannot tell you your individual outcome.

British Council Women in STEM scholarship FAQs

Are British Council Women in STEM scholarships open for 2027?

The sources reviewed do not confirm an open 2027-28 student application round. The British Council confirms that 2026-27 applications have closed. Use a new official announcement, not an old application button, to decide when to apply.

Is the scholarship fully funded?

Yes, the published awards cover tuition and provide support for living and other eligible costs. The previous-cycle figures above show how the package works. Check the university's allowances, payment timing and exclusions rather than treating the total award value as spendable cash.

Can I apply to more than one university?

Yes, the previous South Asia guidance allowed separate applications to multiple universities. Follow each institution’s rules: Queen Mary, for example, instructed candidates to choose one programme within its application process.

Can final-year students apply?

The general 2026-27 criteria allowed universities to consider final-year applicants who could complete their degree before enrolment. Institutions may apply stricter conditions, so ask your chosen university before assuming you qualify.

Is IELTS compulsory?

You must meet the chosen programme’s English requirement. The accepted evidence depends on the institution and course. Scholarship support for an IELTS fee is different from permission to study without an English test.

Can mothers receive additional support?

Brunel’s published package includes a child allowance where applicable, with restrictions. Confirm the relevant university’s conditions and any next-cycle provision before budgeting for a child.

Does this scholarship cover a January 2027 intake?

The sources reviewed do not establish a January 2027 route. An application opening in January and a course starting in January are different events. Check the scholarship’s named academic year and eligible start date.

Other UK scholarships if you are not eligible

Keep your shortlist broader than one award. Applicants from Bangladesh can explore other ways to fund a UK degree from Bangladesh, while Indian applicants can compare other UK awards available to Indian applicants.
